metadata.note: Florida Central and Peninsular Railroad (FC&P), 1889-1900: the Jacksonville-based system formed from the Florida Railway and Navigation Co. - the Western Division to River Junction, Yulee's old Florida Railroad Fernandina - Cedar Key, the Tampa and Orlando lines, and from 1894 the Northern Division to Savannah and the leased South Bound to Columbia, SC. The Seaboard Air Line Railway leased and operated it from 1 July 1900 (merged 15 Aug 1903), so every FC&P feature ends 1900 and the trunk lines continue as separate Seaboard Air Line features (in the SAL colour, pulled from data/) from 1900. Research report: research/branches/florida_central_and_peninsular_railroad.txt.

metadata.ownership_split: Split at 1 July 1900 (SAL lease and operation), not at the 15 Aug 1903 merger. Not split: the 1899 Williams-Middendorf stock purchase (did not change who ran the trains); the 1891 TO&A lease (FC&P already ran Tavares - Orlando trains in Nov 1889). Predecessor operators (Florida Railroad, AG&WIT, Florida Transit, FT&P, FA&GC, P&G/JP&M, FC&W, FR&N, South Bound 1891-92/93, O&WP/EF&A) are not drawn.
branches_deliberately_omitted: St. Marks Branch (Tallahassee - St. Marks): report drawable NONE - no FC&P-era timetable names it.
Columbia - Camden (South Bound extension, 1899-1900): drawable NONE for the FC&P; SAL era belongs to a Seaboard report.
Lake Weir Branch: drawable NONE - no passenger evidence (Fowler itself marks South Lake Weir "pass?").
Sumterville Branch: drawable NONE - no train on a separate branch shown.
Starke - Buda (ASR&G) under the FC&P 1899-1900: drawable NONE; only the SAL 1951 anchor is drawn.
SAL Waldo - Gainesville - Archer - Cedar Key: drawable NONE beyond the takeover year - deferred to a Seaboard Air Line report.

metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing freight-only drawn. Early Bird phosphate branch kept because Fowler dates it in passenger guides 1892-1899; Starke - Bell kept because the 1951 train is a "Mixed" carrying passengers. No OG1952 "freight service only" table found for any ex-FC&P line. Yulee - Fernandina in OG1952 is a bus table and is not used either way.
metadata.horsecar_audit: No animal-powered years drawn. The Tallahassee Rail Road (St. Marks line) was horse/mule drawn before 1856, but that line is not drawn at all.
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] starts: Bronson - Cedar Key 1894 (TT1889 OCR-truncated), Savannah - Columbia 1894 (lease 1892 vs 1893 conflict), Silver Springs 1892, Orlando - Winter Park 1894 (lease 1892 vs merger 1894 conflict), Early Bird 1892.

[OPEN] ends: Early Bird Branch 1899; SAL Jacksonville - Columbia, Jacksonville - Chattahoochee, Jacksonville - Tampa and Wildwood - Orlando all end at 1951, the last CONFIRMED year (Feb 1952 Official Guide), not a known end.
[ANCHOR] single years: Winter Park - Lake Charm 1894, Fernandina - Amelia Beach 1889, SAL Starke - Bell 1951.

FC&P name/start conflict: Wikipedia says the FR&N was reorganized as the FC&P in 1886; railga.com says 1889 (FC&P Railway 1 May 1889). Drawn from 1889, the first FC&P timetable read; 1886-1889 may be FC&P or FR&N.
Plant City - Tampa opening 1890 (marker) vs first timetable proof 1892; drawn from 1892.
Amelia Beach in 1900: abandoned (WP-FCP) or sold and electrified (WP-FAB)?
Waldo - Ocala alignment in the FC&P era: OHM maps an 1879 direct Anthony - Ocala way west of the drawn (present CSX) route via Silver Spring Junction; when the route moved is not established.
FC&P 1890s depots at Jacksonville (Hogan St, to 1896), Orlando (Church St, to 1896) and Tampa were not located; the drawn ends are at later station areas.
Every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh in this file is an estimate.
